notes.text: Blend the hummus in two batches so the blender isn't too full to turn.

move.title: A dip from a can
move.body: Hummus is a chickpea dip eaten all over the Middle East. Today you'll blend it from canned chickpeas, then peel, seed, and slice a cucumber and core and seed tomatoes to go with it, with warm pita.

why.title: Peel away from you
why.body: A vegetable peeler's blade faces the food. Pull it away from your body, with your other hand holding the top end, and the blade never comes toward your fingers.

why.title: Why scoop the seeds
why.body: Cucumber and tomato seeds sit in a watery middle. Scooped out, the slices stay crisp and the plate doesn't get puddles that soak the pita.

why.title: Save the can's liquid
why.body: The liquid in a can of chickpeas is thick and a little salty. A few spoonfuls make hummus smooth and fluffy without watering it down.

why.title: Scrape and blend again
why.body: Thick dips climb the sides of the blender and stop moving. Stopping to scrape them back down gets every chickpea to the blade, so there are no lumps.

why.title: Off and unplugged
why.body: A blender blade is sharper than any knife in the kitchen, and it hides under the food. Turn it off and unplug it before a spatula or a hand goes in the jar.

wrong.sign: The hummus is thick and won't blend
wrong.fix: Add 1 tablespoon of the chickpea liquid, scrape down, and blend again.
Blend it longer, a full minute more, scraping down halfway.
Add a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon, blend, and taste again.
Hold it at a lower angle and use long, steady strokes.

quiz.q: Which way do you pull a peeler?
quiz.explain: The blade never comes toward you.

choices: The slices stay crisp and the plate stays dry
quiz.explain: The seeds sit in a watery middle.

quiz.q: What do you do before putting a spatula in the blender?
choices: Turn it off and unplug it
quiz.explain: The blade hides under the food.

quiz.q: What makes the hummus smooth without watering it down?
choices: The liquid from the chickpea can
quiz.explain: It's thick and a little salty.

substitutions.note: Toast gluten-free bread and cut it into strips for dipping.

steps.text: Turn the oven on to 350°F for the pita.
steps.tip: It heats while you make the hummus.

steps.text: Open the chickpeas. Set the colander over the small bowl and drain them, keeping the liquid.
steps.tip: Keep your fingers away from the lid's cut edge.

steps.text: Put the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt in the blender.
steps.tip: Stir the tahini in its jar first. The oil rises to the top.

steps.text: Add 3 tablespoons of the chickpea liquid and the olive oil. Put the lid on tight.
Blend for 1 minute, with one hand on the lid.
Turn the blender off and unplug it. Scrape down the sides with the spatula.
steps.tip: Unplug it every time a spatula goes in.

steps.text: Plug it back in and blend for 1 more minute. Add more chickpea liquid if it's too thick.
steps.look: Smooth and fluffy, like thick yogurt.

steps.text: Unplug the blender. Taste the hummus on a clean spoon, and add a pinch of salt or lemon if it needs it.
Spoon the hummus onto the plate. Make a swirl with the back of the spoon and sprinkle on the paprika.
steps.tip: A little olive oil in the swirl is traditional.

steps.text: Lay a damp paper towel flat under the cutting board. Rinse the cucumber and tomatoes.
steps.look: Push the board gently. It shouldn't slide.

steps.text: Hold the cucumber by one end on the board. Peel it in long strokes, away from you, turning it as you go.
steps.look: Stripes of green or none, as you like.

steps.text: Trim the ends. Cut the cucumber in half the long way with the paring knife, using the bridge grip.
steps.tip: The knife goes under your hand's bridge.

steps.text: Scrape the seeds out of each half with the tip of a spoon.
steps.look: A clean groove down the middle.

steps.text: Lay the halves flat side down. Slice them into half-moons with the claw grip.
Cut each tomato in half through the stem. Cut a small V around the stem to take out the core.
steps.tip: Point the knife tip away from your hand.

steps.text: Scoop out the seeds with a spoon. Cut each half into wedges.
Set the knife down flat at the top of the board, blade facing away from you.
steps.tip: Do this every time you stop cutting.

steps.text: Lay the pitas on the sheet pan. With oven mitts on, warm them in the oven.
Take the pan out with oven mitts and turn off the oven. Cut each pita into 6 wedges.
steps.tip: Let the pita cool for a minute before you cut it.

steps.text: Arrange the cucumber, tomatoes, olives if you're using them, and pita around the hummus.
steps.tip: Leftover hummus keeps 4 days in a covered container in the fridge.
